speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes. These symptoms together are very concerning for a serious underlying condition. Can you tell me how long you have been experiencing these symptoms, and have you noticed any skin changes or fever?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: That rapid weight loss and night sweats alongside four weeks of worsening pain are alarming. Have you noticed any lumps elsewhere on your body, or any changes in your bowel habits like blood in the stool? Also, have you had any recent fevers?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The fact that the swelling is "fixed" and painless, combined with your B-symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss), strongly suggests a malignancy rather than an infection. REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count with Differential, LDH, and ESR. REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal Ultrasound and CT of the Chest/Abdomen/Pelvis.

Do you have any history of chronic diarrhea, blood in your stool, or a known history of inflammatory bowel disease?

text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Tuberculosis. Given your significant smoking history and the classic presentation of B-symptoms with abdominal pain and supraclavicular lymphadenopathy, this is highly suspicious for disseminated tuberculosis or a tuberculous lymphoma. We must proceed immediately with a PPD test and acid-fast bacilli smear of any aspirated lymph node fluid.
